I'm writing about the Senior Director, US Core Data Domains, Products and Services role. Most of my career has been spent doing exactly this work in pharma - building and governing the commercial data domains that marketing, sales, and market access teams actually rely on - so the shape of this role at Merck is familiar territory rather than a stretch.

At SK Life Science, I ran the data and analytics organization that carried the company from its first US launch through to $1 billion in annual commercial operations. That meant owning HCP/HCO, Product, Vendor, Finance, and Commercial data domains end to end, with formal stewardship and change control built into the ERP, MDM, integration, and analytics layers to satisfy GxP and SOX requirements. Our Snowflake platform, organized in bronze/silver/gold layers, fed roughly 150 production dashboards to about 400 business users across Commercial, Medical Affairs, Finance, and R&D, and self-service adoption grew to around 250 active users on governed Power BI dashboards. I also sponsored a 2025 evaluation of Looker as our next semantic layer, which is the direction I'd expect a group like yours to be pushing toward as well. None of that was theoretical - it was built to serve people who needed reliable numbers on a Monday morning, not a data model that looked good in a slide deck.

On the AI side, I sponsored three solutions that made it into production rather than staying pilots: agent-based automation of first-line security operations that saved an estimated $300,000 to $500,000 a year, an MSL next-best-action model built on Snowflake Cortex that field leadership credited with a marked improvement in engagement, and AI-based expense anomaly detection. Governance mattered as much as the models themselves - validated systems stayed the source of truth, humans reviewed outputs before action, and audit trails were maintained throughout. That discipline is what I'd bring to the RAG pipelines, vector stores, and semantic layers Merck is building toward for its own GenAI-ready infrastructure. On the operational side, I cut technology operating expense by 30 percent through vendor renegotiation, cloud rightsizing, and license consolidation, while holding a zero missed SLA record from 2018 through my departure this year.

My earlier consulting years gave me the domain grounding this posting is looking for - a Product master MDM rollout across 75 countries for AbbVie, HCP/HCO and prescriber mastering work for Eisai, and platform architecture advisory for a range of Reltio's enterprise MDM customers. I'll be candid that the scale I've run most recently sits with an $8 million technology budget and a 38-person organization, smaller than what a company the size of Merck typically carries. What I bring instead is a track record of doing this well at the mid-size end and understanding precisely which of those disciplines - governance structure, domain ownership, cost accountability - scale up cleanly and which need rethinking at enterprise size.

Rahway is a straightforward distance from where I live in Montville, and I'd welcome the chance to talk through how this background maps onto the US Human Health data portfolio you're building. Thank you for considering my application.
